note: mapping_basis=paper_order. data/meloni_2015_disability.py melts the CHIA* columns by name over the parent rows (Protocol 101-199), so the IRW item code IS the source column name (derivation pattern 1, no positional step); the code's suffix (MUSIC/RELIG/SPORT/CULTURAL/SOCIAL) therefore fixes each item's conceptual set outright. What is inferred is the position within a set: the S2 File codebook prints the 25 statements as one flat roman-numbered list (i)..(xxv) tied to no variable code. That list falls into runs of 3 music / 5 religious / 5 sport / 4 cultural / 8 social, which matches the live per-suffix code counts exactly (3/5/5/4/8 of 25), and the 25 CHIA columns appear in the S1 workbook in precisely that same order (CHIA1-3_MUSIC, CHIA1-5_RELIG, CHIA1-5_SPORT, CHIA1-4_CULTURAL, CHIA1-8_SOCIAL, columns 0-24 of the CHIA block), so only order within a block is an assumption. NO data_labels route exists: the S1 .xls is an SPSS export carrying bare column names only, no variable or value labels - opened and checked. OPTION TEXT IS A DEVIATION worth reading twice: the codebook states only 'Scale: Important/Not Important from 1 to 5' and labels no individual scale point, so 'Not Important' at resp 1 and 'Important' at resp 5 are the codebook's own two pole words placed by this project; resp 2-4 are left blank rather than padded. The placement is corroborated by the data (see verify_meloni_2015_parent_interests.R): reading books (mean 4.46) and practising sport (4.24) sit at the top and watching sport on television (1.96) at the bottom, which is only possible if 5 is the 'Important' pole. LANGUAGE: interviews were conducted in Italian in participants' homes by author Fabio Meloni; the deposit publishes only S1 (data) and S2 (measures) and neither contains any Italian - s002.txt has zero accented characters and the .xls has no string columns at all - so text_source=translated_substitute with the study's own English in the base fields and the _translated columns empty, per the 2026-09-01 fallback.
